description:
## Goal

Give every logical source publisher one stable typed `SourceOwner` and every exact name/text/provenance instance one immutable `SourceVersion`. Owner identity answers “which publisher?”; version identity answers “which exact source bytes produced this diagnostic location?” This is the initial identity cutover for ordinary submissions, reserved runtime sources, preludes, and macro-mediated publication. It does not expose live replacement.

## Final model

- Source-publisher jobs, declarations, facts, and lexical ownership use `SourceOwner`.
- Tokens, quoted-node metadata, and diagnostic `Span` use `SourceVersion`.
- `SourceMap` is the sole immutable name/text/provenance authority. `CodeMap` retains only owner publication state pointing at the current immutable version; it has no parallel name/text columns.
- Runtime owners are reserved at bootstrap and materialize source text exactly once, on demand.
- Source-less synthetic/global state is explicit absence. No dummy owner or fake version exists.
- Mixed macro output retains definition and caller versions on the nodes that actually came from each source. Macro publication retains its lexical owner.
- Every untrusted quoted AST node is acquired through `ast_node(&SourceMap)`, which validates its own metadata and returns its resolved optional span. The raw span decoder is private and single-use. Missing metadata remains absent/DUMMY; malformed metadata is an error and is never repaired, restamped from a parent, or reclassified as a shape mismatch. The only production bypass is a narrow frontdoor call-shape check over metadata it just built; test inspection is cfg(test).
- Generated callable code identity is separate from diagnostic provenance. Final quoted-function decoding assigns each lambda one immutable structural `LambdaOccurrence` through its existing recursive traversal. `FunctionMap` combines that occurrence with its owner’s shared `FunctionDenotation`; `Types` and runtime consume the same denotation. Diagnostic `Span` remains on the function surface. No second callable-order identity, span-derived peer mint, raw source/function id, filename, display string, hash, or mint order is authority.
- Named module/function/type identities remain typed semantic identities. Explicit source/prelude order keeps its language meaning; incidental owner/version allocation cannot change semantic answers or canonical artifacts.

## TDD signal

The production path proves stable owners and immutable versions for named, unnamed, runtime, and prelude sources; exact diagnostic resolution; mixed definition/caller macro provenance; source-less interpreter/JIT parity; malformed ordinary, nested-wrapper, remote-callee, sugar, and token provenance rejection; and cold runtime reservation without source materialization.

Generated-callable tests prove same structural occurrence rereference is idempotent, distinct and nested structural occurrences remain owner-relative, unrelated function allocation does not move typed ordering or canonical bytes, and two source-less macro expansions of delayed values evaluate `20 + 22` as `42` rather than conflating both generated bodies into `44`.

## Cutover and deletion

Replace compiler `CodeId` with opaque `SourceOwner` and old `source::Id` with opaque `SourceVersion` in one live cut. Delete source/code ordinal coincidence, `CodeId::from_source`, duplicate CodeMap name/text storage, dummy/detached source identities, filename/display inference, eager native quote scanning, source-version reconstruction, and compatibility identity paths. Integrate with `.27`’s existing typed `FunctionDenotation`/`LambdaOccurrence` authority; delete the superseded replay’s parallel `GeneratedFunctionOccurrence` and `CallableOrderIdentity` instead of preserving them.

No source mirror, replacement history, rollback state, reconciliation pass, eager graph validation, submit adapter, or live replacement API is introduced. Location-independent replacement remains `fz-tfn.57`; broader executable/provenance separation remains `fz-tfn.40`.

## Accepted evidence

Accepted rewritten commit: `dd23b98cc` (`fz-tfn.61: give every source one stable owner and immutable version`) on parent `19f6db4cb`, itself stacked on `fz-lib` `fb04be432`.

Reviewed binary diff SHA-256: `7eb43d34e6661e15443547a20ea4dc1378b70b5ac56e6420a1eb8da738250718` (77 files, +3,249/−1,816). The smaller replay is intentional: `.27` already owns typed callable denotation and structural lambda occurrence, so `.61` retains only source owner/version/provenance work and deletes its obsolete parallel identity machinery.

Final integrated gates: 2,033 library tests passed / 6 ignored / 0 failed; 676/676 serial fixture cases; 30/30 CLI cases; 257 runtime tests; AOT variadic; doctests; workspace all-target/all-feature check; strict Clippy with warnings denied; formatting and diff checks. PR #122 was green before the rewritten stack was pushed; GitHub Actions run `34301389706` is the exact-head CI for the four-commit PR #125 stack.

A fresh Astra-high ticket-scoped review inspected every one of the 23 semantic conflict seams against the original acceptance criteria and `.27` authorities, ran 66 focused provenance/identity tests, and approved the exact staged hash without blockers. No temporary artifacts, migration adapters, duplicate comparator, reconstruction path, or callable-order side authority remain.

## Unblocks

- `fz-tfn.53` publishes each validated source contribution as one typed batch.
title: Give every source one stable owner and immutable version
